athletic director position, reduced to 0.5 FTE (split from vice principal role)

statements.statement: Chapter 70 aid increased $135,915 in the FY27 final state budget versus the governor's initial proposal
Charter tuition reimbursement increased $116,413 in the FY27 final state budget versus the governor's proposal
Smart growth school reimbursement increased, figure given as $160,187,000 in the FY27 final state budget
Total increase in FY27 cherry sheet receipts (state aid) versus the governor's initial proposal was $491,988
Extra state assessments and charges (charter and school-choice sending tuition) increased $15,326 in the FY27 final budget
Net additional state aid to Lunenburg after subtracting extra assessments is $476,662
The school committee cut over $800,000 from the FY27 school budget
The town's stabilization fund holds over $9 million; a member said she is not requesting any of that money for this appropriation
School committee's original warrant article, voted at the prior meeting, requested an additional $350,000 for the FY27 school operating budget
A member suggested the school could instead request $475,000, the town's entire cherry sheet increase, rather than the smaller figure
School committee voted to amend its FY27 warrant article to request an additional $418,056 for the school operating budget, to go before the September 3 special town meeting
A member clarified this additional funding request is not an override and will not raise the tax rate; it is state money already collected being returned to the town
Governor proposed an additional $100 million statewide, from millionaire's-tax revenue, for a per-pupil funding increase, pending legislative passage (House 5586)
Potential additional state funding to the district under the per-pupil proposal was estimated at $170,000, described as very much TBD
A member said the potential $175,000 per-pupil funding is not enough to restore four teacher positions
